
'''{{ill|Isurugi Gongen|ja|石動権現}}''' (いするぎごんげん) is a deity of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|en|Shinbutsu-shūgō|qid=Q2279088|lt=Shinbutsu-shūgō}} that emerged from the fusion of the {{ill|Mountain worship|en|Mountain worship|qid=Q93697439|lt=Mountain Worship}} and {{ill|Shugendō|en|Shugendō|qid=Q1483875|lt=Shugendō}} traditions of {{ill|Noto Province|en|Noto Province|qid=Q1047671|lt=Noto Province}} and {{ill|Mount Sekidō|en|Mount Sekidō|qid=Q11585200|lt=Isurugi Mountain}}. It enshrines {{ill|Ākāśagarbha|en|Ākāśagarbha|qid=Q416174|lt=Kokūzō Bosatsu}} as its {{ill|Honji suijaku|en|Honji suijaku|qid=Q3080781|lt=Honji Buddha}}, and before the implementation of {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|en|Shinbutsu bunri|qid=Q1970535|lt=Separation of Shinto and Buddhism}} and {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|en|Haibutsu kishaku|qid=Q702298|lt=Haibutsu kishaku}}, it was venerated at the various '''Isurugi Shrines''' after being invited from {{ill|Isurugi Mountain Tenpyō Temple|ja|石動山天平寺}}.

== Overview ==
According to the ''Isurugi Mountain Ancient Origins'' (『石動山古縁起』), in the 6th year of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}, the hermit {{ill|Hōdō Sennin|ja|方道仙人}} opened the mountain, and in the first year of the {{ill|Yōrō era|ja|養老元年}} ({{ill|717|en|717|qid=Q23532|lt=717}}), the monk {{ill|Chitoku Shōnin|ja|智徳上人}} ascended it and, in the 8th year of {{ill|Tenpyō-shōhō|en|Tenpyō-shōhō|qid=Q1373169|lt=Tenpyō Shōhō}} ({{ill|756|en|756|qid=Q31121|lt=756}}), constructed the Great Ceremonial Hall (lecture hall). On the other hand, a founding tradition attributed to {{ill|Taichō|en|Taichō|qid=Q2388439|lt=Taichō}} has long existed, and the ''Shin Enki'' (『新縁起』) authored by {{ill|Hayashi Razan|en|Hayashi Razan|qid=Q558279|lt=Hayashi Razan}} in the early modern period also asserts that it was established by Taichō.

In the Middle Ages, ''Isurugi Shugyō'' reached its zenith, with {{ill|Isurugi Mountain Tenpyō Temple|ja|石動山天平寺}} counting over 360 establishments and 3,000 followers.

== Separation of Shinto and Buddhism and Haibutsu Kishaku ==
Due to the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離令|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1970535|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1970535}} issued during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|en|Meiji Restoration|qid=Q8707|lt=Meiji Restoration}}, the Shugendō-based {{ill|Isurugi Gongen|ja|石動権現}} was abolished. In the 3rd year of {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} ({{ill|1870|en|1870|qid=Q7741|lt=1870}}), the Shingon temple {{ill|Isurugi Mountain Tenpyō Temple|ja|石動山天平寺}} was forced into abeyance and reorganized as the {{ill|Isurugi Hikojinja|ja|伊須流岐比古神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11381009}} ({{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|en|Ishikawa Prefecture|qid=Q131281|lt=Ishikawa Prefecture}}). Many of the Isurugi shrines nationwide have since become Shinto shrines or Five-Shrine complexes enshrining {{ill|Isurugi Hiko|ja|伊須流岐比古神|qid=Q140446114|lt=Isurugi Hiko}} and others as their deities.
